question: Can the same-release current/prior Exhibit 7 Semiconductors pair avoid cross-vintage revisions, and where does the officially announced January 2012 end-use reclassification break comparability? This is a source-semantics audit before any Stage1 factor fit.
method: Verify every original PDF's SHA-256 and size against its saved row audit. For all 188 source months, inspect the first five physical PDF pages for exact case-insensitive phrases 'Changes to End-Use Commodity Classification', 'semiconductor media', 'reassigned', and 'Harmonized System'; retain page, source hash and bounded context. Compare each same-release prior-month Semiconductors value with the preceding report's current-month value only as a revision diagnostic, never as a factor. Visually inspect 2011-12, 2012-01 and 2012-02 Exhibit 7 and notice pages separately. No market labels or model outcomes.
preidentified_boundary: The 2012-02 release notice says end-use commodity reclassification is effective with January 2012 statistics and moves smart cards and flash memory cards into semiconductors and related devices. Until a same-basis original bridge is shown, the 2012-01 month-over-month Semiconductors growth across December 2011 is unknown. Later same-release current/prior pairs require separate audit for additional notices and revisions.
limits: Current downloads of historical PDF URLs do not by themselves certify their bytes were the first public versions. A same-release monthly pair reduces cross-release revision mixing but does not prove timing, economic predictiveness, or full account value.
stop: Any source SHA/size mismatch, duplicate month, missing row, or unresolved new classification notice stops factor qualification. Preserve all months and unknown transitions; do not fit or tune from SOXX returns.
